name: Alloy
summary: Daniel Jackson's lightweight formal specification language based on first-order relational logic with transitive closure ('everything is a relation'); the Alloy Analyzer finds instances and counterexamples within bounded scopes by translating models to SAT through Kodkod. Alloy 6 (2021) adds mutable signatures/fields and linear temporal logic from Electrum.

level_notes.1: No external standard. The online Alloy Language Reference (alloytools.org/spec.html, derived from Appendix B of Software Abstractions) together with the CUP grammar in the Analyzer repository define the language; Jackson's TOSEM 2002 paper defines the original (Alloy 2) semantics. Alloy 6 temporal extensions are documented on alloytools.org/alloy6.html.
level_notes.0: The Alloy Analyzer (Java, AlloyTools/org.alloytools.alloy) is the reference implementation: JFlex/CUP front end, AST in edu.mit.csail.sdg.ast, translation to the Kodkod relational model finder, which emits SAT problems. Forge (Brown) and Electrum are derived implementations.
level_notes.2: Software Abstractions (MIT Press, 2006/2012) is paywalled; the free online books Formal Software Design with Alloy 6 and Practical Alloy, plus Hillel Wayne's community docs, are linked section by section.
